children: Subhayan Chakraborty New Delhi: India's semiconductor mission, the second iteration of which was launched recently, is much more comprehensive than many other countries, Infineon Technologies CEO Jochen Hanebeck told ET. "We are studying it closely.

Compared to many other countries, it's more comprehensive and thought through. It leverages the current capabilities of India, including chip designing, and software development. It now goes into many other parts of the value chain. It's good to address the full value chain, from materials to equipment, assembly, startups and talent," he said.

The German integrated device manufacturer is the largest producer of chips for the power and automotive segment globally. It also operates 14 fabrication plants worldwide. A key growth market for Infineon with 1,200 customers, India is targeted to make up Rs 800 million in sales by 2030, with a 30% compounded annual growth rate. "Automotives are currently the largest category among sales. However, the fastest growth will be from everything around power infrastructure - generation, transmission, storage. Here we will try to benefit from the drive towards electrification of the country," he said.

title: Infineon's CEO Lauds India's 'Thought Through' Chip Plan
